title: Neural network quantization
text: Quantization reduces the memory footprint and compute cost of a neural network by representing weights and activations with fewer bits, for example 8-bit integers instead of 32-bit floating point numbers. Post-training quantization converts an already trained model, while quantization-aware training simulates low precision during training to recover accuracy. The trade-off is a small accuracy loss in exchange for models that are roughly four times smaller and faster on edge hardware.

title: Gradient descent
text: Gradient descent is an iterative optimization algorithm that minimizes a loss function by repeatedly moving the parameters in the direction of the negative gradient. The learning rate controls the step size: too large a value makes training diverge, too small a value makes it slow. Stochastic gradient descent estimates the gradient from a small random mini-batch of examples, which makes each update cheap and adds helpful noise.

title: Attention is all you need
text: The Transformer architecture replaces recurrence with self-attention. Each token computes attention weights over all other tokens in the sequence, so long-range dependencies are modelled in a single step and training parallelizes well on GPUs. Multi-head attention lets the model attend to information from different representation subspaces. The Transformer was introduced in 2017 for machine translation.

title: Retrieval-augmented generation
text: Retrieval-augmented generation combines a retriever with a language model. Relevant passages are retrieved from an external corpus and given to the generator as context, which grounds the answer in sources and reduces hallucination. Hybrid retrieval mixes dense embedding search with sparse lexical search such as BM25 to improve recall on both semantic and keyword queries.

title: BM25 ranking function
text: BM25 is a lexical ranking function that scores documents by the query terms they contain. It weights each term by its inverse document frequency and applies term frequency saturation and document length normalization. BM25 is strong on exact keyword matches such as rare technical terms and identifiers, where dense embeddings can fail.

title: Overfitting and regularization
text: Overfitting happens when a model memorizes the training data and fails to generalize to unseen data. Regularization techniques such as weight decay, dropout and early stopping reduce overfitting. A held-out validation set is used to detect it: training loss keeps decreasing while validation loss starts to increase.

title: Batch normalization
text: Batch normalization normalizes the activations of a layer using the mean and variance of the current mini-batch, followed by a learned scale and shift. It stabilizes and accelerates the training of deep networks and allows higher learning rates. At inference time running averages of the statistics are used instead of batch statistics.

title: Low-rank adaptation
text: Low-rank adaptation, or LoRA, fine-tunes a large language model by freezing the pretrained weights and training small low-rank update matrices injected into selected layers. This reduces the number of trainable parameters by orders of magnitude and cuts memory usage, making fine-tuning feasible on a single consumer GPU.
